conversations.answer: The issue you're facing where the last flex item in a row overflows to the next row is because of how the browser calculates the width of flex items and rounding issues. Your temporary solution of subtracting 1 from theGridItself.clientWidth is a common approach to deal with this problem. However, there's another way to solve this issue without hardcoding the -1. You can use calc to calculate the width with a percentage-based approach.Here's how you can modify your drawGrid function to use the calc method:[CODE_BLOCK_0]By setting flexBasis to calc(100% / ${squareSideSize}), you're telling the browser to divide the container's width into equal parts based on the squareSideSize without needing to subtract 1. This should prevent the last item in a row from overflowing to the next row and give you a more accurate grid layout.This approach is more flexible because it adapts automatically to changes in container size and doesn't rely on hardcoded values.
